The Poisoner — Disaster Inc. (situational)

Status: Active — possesses poisoned daggers of unusual potency

Roger is the person whose poisoned dagger caused Earl Grey to literally explode during the Syndicate Showdown. The poison's interaction with Earl Grey's physiology was completely unexpected and remains unexplained. Roger has carried poisoned weapons throughout the campaign, which makes him valuable in combat and EXTREMELY concerning in any situation where accidental poisoning is a possibility. Waluigi stands at least ten feet away from Roger at all times.

Evidence

  • Dagger — “Active — possesses poisoned daggers of unusual potency”
  • Sneak Attack — “The Poisoner”

The Man Who Jumped — Liberated Toads / Disaster Inc. (separated)

Status: Active — location uncertain, last known contact with Rakasha spirit-walkers

Ryan is the person who jumped off the Vigilance during the Iron Sky Breach rather than be captured by the Iron Legion. He jumped. Off an airship. In the sky. He survived—somehow—and was taken in by a Rakasha spirit-walker. Waluigi does not know Ryan's current status or location, but anyone who survives a jump like that has earned Waluigi's respect forever.

Evidence

  • Spear — “The Man Who Jumped”
  • Iron Discipline — “Ryan is the person who jumped off the Vigilance during the Iron Sky Breach rather than be captured by the Iron Legion.”

The Venomous Casualty — Disaster Inc. (situational)

Status: Active — recovering from spider venom

Smoking J was bitten during the Battle of the Spider Grove and suffered a severe venomous reaction that forced his withdrawal from the front line. His incapacitation at a critical moment reduced the party's fighting strength during the most dangerous phase of the battle. Waluigi hopes Smoking J has fully recovered, though the long-term effects of arachnid venom are unpredictable.

Evidence

  • Bite — “He was fighting alongside the main group when one of the dog-sized spiders landed a bite.”
  • Pack Tactics — “The toad squad got cut off partly because there weren't enough fighters to maintain a continuous line.”
  • Mechanical Aptitude — “Remi had to hold her position with only her mechanical dog as backup.”

description.value:
Wondrous item, (requires attunement)

Originally a gift from his family, Usk modified it with a silver raven's skull clasp to honor the Corvinarus family he was serving with.

The cloak is light, and meant to mimic that of a raven's feathers. Its most unique quality is how it quiets the movements of the wearer, making it harder for others to hear them when they are carrying out tasks.

Attempts to detect the wearer while doing a noisy task (picking locks, rifling through a drawer, drawing a dagger, etc) have disadvantage. This does not apply to combat actions or movement.

biography.value:
Wario's Motorbike

Wario's customized motorcycle — purple with yellow accents and a large "W" emblem on the gas tank — is his primary getaway vehicle when Warp Pipes are not available or practical. It is loud, obnoxious, and belches black smoke; it can be heard coming from half a mile away, which somewhat defeats the purpose of a getaway vehicle. Wario refuses to acknowledge this flaw.

Field record — The Scorncrow Skirmish. Wario arrived on this motorbike roaring "You want fun? Wario show you fun!" at the overgrown grove — and the motorbike stalled, caught fast in the leaves and branches before it had travelled the length of its own entrance. It remains stalled in the undergrowth, and Waluigi files the motorbike retrieval fee as pending.

Specifications. AC 16 (reinforced frame with armor plating), 75 hit points, damage threshold 10 (attacks dealing less than 10 damage do not harm it), speed 120 feet per round (roughly 80 mph at full throttle), crew 1 driver and 1 passenger (uncomfortably), cargo 200 pounds in the rear compartment. The bike runs on "Wario Fuel" — a proprietary blend that smells like garlic, burns purple, and is probably illegal in most jurisdictions; Wario has never actually bought fuel for it, and it never seems to run out.

Waluigi's machine reference sheet for the motorbike is filed with the skirmish record. It is a machine-rendered study, so its maroon paint job is not canon; the item record says purple with yellow accents.

Other records of the same machine. Wario's sheet carries this machine twice: as a customized motorcycle (the block above) and as a weaponized "Custom Chopper" configuration (AC 16, 75 HP, speed 70 ft; forward-facing flamethrower, spiked wheel guards, and an oil slick dispenser). His Wario Bike Summon feat uses a simpler summoned-mount block (AC 14, 50 HP, speed 60 ft). This actor is the physical customized motorcycle.
biography.public: A customized purple-and-yellow motorcycle with a large "W" on the gas tank, armored plating, and saddlebags. It is currently stalled in the undergrowth of the overgrown grove.

description.value: Wario drives the motorbike directly into a creature or object. Make an attack roll using the driver's Strength modifier + proficiency bonus (this vehicle has no ability scores of its own, so the item rolls flat here). On a hit the target takes 4d10 bludgeoning damage, and the driver must succeed on a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw or be thrown from the bike, taking 2d6 bludgeoning damage and landing prone 10 feet away. The motorbike takes half the damage dealt to the target.

unidentified.name: Ramming Vehicle
unidentified.description: A heavy motorcycle hurled at full throttle.

description.value: Damage Threshold 10. Attacks dealing less than 10 damage do not harm the motorbike because of its reinforced frame and armor plating. AC is 16.

Once per short rest, Wario can activate the illegal nitrous oxide injectors. For 1 minute the motorbike's speed doubles to 240 feet per round, but handling becomes extremely difficult: all vehicle maneuver checks are made with disadvantage, and there is a 20% chance each round that the engine overheats, forcing a stop for 1d4 rounds while it cools down.

As a bonus action, the modified exhaust releases thick black smoke, filling a 20-foot cube behind the motorbike with heavily obscuring smoke that lasts 1 minute or until dispersed by strong wind. Used exclusively to escape pursuers or cover criminal activity — never for legitimate purposes.

The bike runs on "Wario Fuel": a blend that smells like garlic, burns purple, and is probably illegal in most jurisdictions. Some say it is garlic oil, others suspect pure greed. Wario has never bought fuel for it, and it never seems to actually run out. If reduced to 0 HP, it can be resummoned after a long rest, emerging dented and smoking but functional.

A mounted horn that plays a jarring "WAH HA HA HA!" when honked, which Wario uses constantly and inappropriately. The bike has been banned from at least seven cities for noise violations, emissions standards breaches, and general obnoxiousness.

Wario's sheet also records a weaponized configuration of this machine as Wario's Custom Chopper (Weaponized Motorcycle) (AC 16, 75 HP, speed 70 ft, rare). It replaces the customizations above with: a forward-facing flamethrower (bonus action, 15-foot cone, DC 14 Dexterity save, 2d6 fire damage); spiked wheel guards (creatures hit by ramming attacks take an extra 1d6 piercing damage); and an oil slick dispenser (action, 30-foot line of difficult terrain lasting 1 minute, DC 14 Dexterity save or fall prone). Use this block when the scene calls for the weaponized build, not this one.

A secret compartment under the seat. A DC 18 Intelligence (Investigation) check finds it if you do not know it is there. It holds emergency funds (currently 500 gp), a backup Warp Pipe activator, and what Wario describes as "insurance documents" — actually blackmail material on various business partners.
